artifacts.summary: Reachability probe design (ps+/proc, ~35ms, no spawn) and a routing-architecture finding: /orchestrate bypasses the 4 lean skills' Stage 2 entirely, and the manifest hooks.preflight mechanism is task_type-keyed so it cannot reach a lean-owned hook for the formal-typed incident that motivated this task; fix must be an unconditional, directory-gated call from orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh. .olean staleness excluded from scope (belongs with task 268 / Lake's own build cache, not a sub-100ms preflight).

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, /orchestrate resolves agents directly via command-route-agent.sh/orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh and never executes the body of the per-domain SKILL.md files (e.g. skill-lean-research). Any inline Stage 2/3 logic hand-written in those SKILL.md files (status updates aside, which are reimplemented via skill_preflight_update) is dead code on the /orchestrate path and only fires on a direct /research|/plan|/implement invocation. A fix intended to affect /orchestrate dispatches must land in orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh or orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, not in a skill body.

skill_run_extension_hook (skill-base.sh) resolves a manifest hooks.* entry by task_type -> single owning extension (skill_get_extension_dir). A hook declared on extension A never fires for a dispatch whose task_type is owned by extension B, even if B's project happens to depend on A's domain (e.g. a 'formal' task_type proving theorems in Lean never reaches a hook declared in the 'lean' extension's manifest, since 'formal' depends only on 'core'). Any cross-domain preflight signal that must fire regardless of task_type needs an unconditional, directory/content-detection-gated call from a script every dispatch passes through (e.g. orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh), not a manifest hooks.preflight registration.

Cheap, no-spawn MCP server reachability probe technique: uvx does not exec-replace itself, so a spawned 'uvx <pkg>' server always shows as two ps rows (a 'uv' launcher and the real interpreter/script child), making comm-based matching useless (multiple uv-launched MCP servers share comm=uv) -- match on an args substring naming the package instead. Once a candidate PID is found, /proc/<pid>/environ and /proc/<pid>/cwd give an exact (not heuristic) cross-check against an expected per-project path (e.g. LEAN_PROJECT_PATH). Measured cost on this machine: ~35ms for one ps snapshot plus the /proc reads -- Linux-only (no /proc on macOS; degrade to an explicit 'unknown' tier there, never silently 'reachable').
